evidence.observation: D4 proposes: "Five: roster cap (default 128, ceiling 4,096), largest budget (1 MiB, 64 MiB), per-file input (128 KiB, 8 MiB), response (64 KiB, 1 MiB), route timeout (30 s, 600 s)", while §2 LH1 binds the limits argument as "fields of one limits argument, each with a default equal to today's constant and a hard ceiling (D4, R0.8)". In the repository, no 64 KiB response-cap constant exists: reading.py reads every file through depth.py's `_read` (`return read_regular_bounded(root, name, max_bytes=INPUT_LIMIT)[0]` at depth.py:56 with `INPUT_LIMIT = 128 * 1024` at depth.py:21), and `_inspect` (reading.py:167-195) applies no size bound to a response beyond that file-read cap. The other four defaults match real constants (ROSTER_LIMIT=128 reading.py:41, MAX_BUDGET=1<<20 reading.py:40, INPUT_LIMIT 128 KiB, timeout_seconds=30 depth.py:24); only the response default has no corresponding "today's constant".

concerns.recommendation: Amend D4 (at the plan gate or in the LH1 spec, flagged as a deviation) so the response-cap default equals a real present bound - 128 KiB, the per-file read cap that today limits responses.json - or drop the 'default equal to today's constant' claim for this one cap, keeping R0.2's packaged-bytes guarantee in mind.
concerns.title: D4's response-cap default (64 KiB) matches no constant in the code, contradicting the plan's own defaults rule

evidence.location: §10 D6 (line 414) and §2 LH1 "Per document" (lines 194-198) vs §4 LH1 criteria (line 308)
evidence.observation: The owner-ruled D6 row states: "A byte budget per source, enforced in the loop, and a stop reason per source in the report. A document whose required questions are resolved still gets its other scheduled reads", and §2 LH1 repeats "A document whose required questions are resolved still gets its other scheduled reads (D6, ruled `(o)`)". Yet no LH1 criterion tests this ruled clause: LH1-C5 only holds "a document budget ends one document and not the other; each source has its stop reason", and no other LH1 criterion (C1-C13, line 308) exercises continuation after required coverage resolves. Compare the other rulings, each of which has a criterion (D9/D17: LH3-C1 and LH3-C10; D10: LH3-C2). §11 confirms "no criterion changes" for D6, so the gap is plan-wide, not spec-deferred.

concerns.recommendation: Add one clause to LH1-C5 (or a new criterion) holding that a document whose required questions are resolved still receives its other scheduled reads, so the owner-ruled half of D6 is verified rather than only the budget half.
concerns.title: The D6 ruling's 'resolved questions still get scheduled reads' clause has no acceptance criterion

evidence.location: §0 R0.8 (lines 93-95) vs §4 LH1-C10 (line 308) and §6 risk table (line 352)
evidence.observation: R0.8 binds: "Each cap that becomes a parameter has a hard maximum fixed in its spec, and a time-bound test at that maximum (standing rule 2)." D4 makes five caps parameters, but the only LH1 timing criterion is LH1-C10: "Inputs at each roster ceiling load within the spec's time bound", which names only roster ceilings and says nothing about the budget (64 MiB), per-file input (8 MiB), response (1 MiB) or route-timeout (600 s) ceilings. The §6 risk row "A raised cap turns a legal input into minutes of CPU" names "R0.8; LH1-C10, LH3-C9" as its control, so the plan leans on LH1-C10 to cover all five raised caps while the criterion as written covers at most one.

concerns.recommendation: Widen LH1-C10 (or add one criterion) so a time-bound test exists at each of the five D4 ceilings, as R0.8 requires, or state in the LH1 spec which ceilings share one bound test and why.
concerns.title: R0.8 requires a time-bound test at every cap's maximum, but LH1-C10 names only roster ceilings

Three hardening concerns: D4's proposed 64 KiB response-cap default matches no constant in the code (today's effective bound is the 128 KiB per-file read cap), contradicting the binding rule that defaults equal today's constants; the D6 ruling's continuation clause has no acceptance criterion; and R0.8's time-bound-at-maximum rule is only partially covered by LH1-C10. No blocking concerns; the phases are specifiable, implementable and testable as written.
